aldric_miller.name: Aldric
aldric_miller.personality: Quiet, methodical, oddly philosophical about grain
aldric_miller.appearance: Flour-dusted, large hands, always seems to be listening to something you can't hear
signature_questions: You know, some folk want their flour fine as dust — almost powder. Others want it rough, with texture you can feel. I find that says something about a person. Which do you prefer?
The wheel turns whether I'm here or not. Does that comfort you, or does it bother you?
I had a traveler once ask me why I bother grinding grain when you could just eat the whole kernel. I didn't have an answer. What would you have said?

marta_innkeeper.name: Marta
marta_innkeeper.personality: Warm, sharp-eyed, remembers everything everyone has ever said to her
marta_innkeeper.appearance: Round-faced, always drying her hands on an apron that never gets clean
signature_questions: We had a traveler last month who insisted on sleeping with the window open despite the cold. Said he needed to hear the world outside. Do you find yourself listening for things?
I sometimes wonder — if someone you trusted lied to you to protect you, would you want to know?
My daughter says I remember too much. That I should let things go. I think I remember exactly the right amount. Which are you?

cob_guard.name: Cob
cob_guard.personality: Practical, carries a guilt he doesn't talk about, weirdly relieved to see strangers
cob_guard.appearance: Broad shoulders, a nose that's been broken twice, always leaning on something
signature_questions: Between you and me — I let a thief go last season. Caught him stealing bread for his kids. Still wonder sometimes if I did right. What would you have done?
Rules are rules, but rules don't always account for people. You seem like someone who's had to decide which matters more.
I've been guard here twelve years. Never had to draw my sword. Is that a good thing or a wasted life?

elowen_herbalist.name: Elowen
elowen_herbalist.personality: Precise, patient, sorts plants by a system only she understands
elowen_herbalist.appearance: Long fingers perpetually stained green, talks to plants under her breath
signature_questions: Some people want a remedy fast — they don't care how it works, only that it does. Others want to understand every step. Which are you?
I grow things that won't bloom here. Keep trying anyway. Some would call that foolish. What do you call it?
There's a plant that only survives by making itself taste terrible. I've always found that an interesting solution. Is that admirable or sad?

nessa_merchant.name: Nessa
nessa_merchant.personality: Fast-talking, shrewd, never stays long but always comes back
nessa_merchant.appearance: Colorful scarves, rings on every finger, eyes that calculate faster than she speaks
signature_questions: I sell information sometimes. Not secrets — just things people overlook. Would you buy that, or does it feel wrong to you?
I once told a customer their horse was overpriced when I could have stayed quiet and sold them something else. I lost coin that day. Was that stupid or decent?
People think merchants only care about gold. Some of us care about the story of how the gold moves. Do you see money as a means or a story?

ysabel_elder.name: Ysabel
ysabel_elder.personality: Ancient, unhurried, asks questions like she already knows the answers
ysabel_elder.appearance: Wrapped in shawls regardless of weather, hands folded over a carved walking stick she never uses
signature_questions: I dreamed of you last night. You were standing in fire. Were you running toward it or away from it?
My grandson asked me yesterday why I help strangers. I couldn't think of a good answer. What would you have said?
If you could be invisible for one day — truly unseen — what would you do? And please, don't tell me what you think you should say.

finn_acolyte.name: Finn
finn_acolyte.personality: Young, uncertain of his faith, deeply curious about everyone else's certainty
finn_acolyte.appearance: Too-large robes, ink-stained fingers, always in the middle of a thought
signature_questions: I take care of this chapel but I'm not sure I believe in anything it stands for. Is that dishonest, or just honest?
People come here when they're lost. They leave the same way they arrived, mostly. But sometimes not. What do you come to places like this looking for?
If you knew something terrible about someone who was also being kind to you — would knowing it change how you received the kindness?
